You are a planning expert. Given an asynchronous planning problem, extract the dependency graph.

For each step, identify:
1. A short snake_case name (e.g., "boil_water", "add_pasta") — use ONLY lowercase letters, digits, and underscores
2. The duration in SECONDS (convert minutes/hours/days if needed: 1 min=60s, 1 hour=3600s, 1 day=86400s)
3. The DIRECT predecessors — steps that MUST complete before this step can start

CRITICAL RULES:
- List ALL direct predecessor steps in "depends_on". A missing dependency will cause a wrong answer.
- If a step has no prerequisites, use an empty list [].
- Every name in "depends_on" MUST exactly match a "name" defined in the same "steps" list.
- Capture ONLY dependencies stated in the problem. Do NOT add extra constraints.

SELF-CHECK before returning:
1. Re-read EVERY ordering constraint in the problem. Is each one captured in some step's "depends_on"?
2. For every entry in any "depends_on" list, confirm that exact name appears as a "name" in the steps list.

Return JSON with key "responses" (list of dicts). Each dict must have key "steps" (list of step dicts).
Each step dict must include:
- "name": snake_case string identifier
- "duration": integer seconds
- "depends_on": list of step name strings (direct predecessors only)

Example:
{
  "responses": [{
    "steps": [
      {"name": "boil_water",  "duration": 300,  "depends_on": []},
      {"name": "add_pasta",   "duration": 600,  "depends_on": ["boil_water"]},
      {"name": "make_sauce",  "duration": 900,  "depends_on": []},
      {"name": "combine",     "duration": 60,   "depends_on": ["add_pasta", "make_sauce"]}
    ]
  }]
}

Here is an asynchronous planning problem.

To send a letter, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Seal the envelope securely (30 seconds)
Step 2. Write the recipient's street address (45 seconds)
Step 3. Double-check the recipient's zip code (60 seconds)

Step 5. Weigh the envelope for postage (60 seconds)
Step 6. Walk to the neighborhood blue mailbox (600 seconds)
Step 7. Select a clean sheet of stationery (20 seconds)
Step 8. Write the date at the top of the letter (15 seconds)
Step 9. Write the formal salutation (10 seconds)
Step 10. Draft the introductory paragraph (300 seconds)

Step 12. Decide on the main message of the letter (600 seconds)
Step 13. Write the body of the letter (900 seconds)
Step 14. Add a postscript at the bottom (60 seconds)
Step 15. Find a comfortable pen that works (120 seconds)
Step 16. Fold the letter into thirds (20 seconds)

Step 18. Sign your name at the end (15 seconds)
Step 19. Retrieve the recipient's address from your contacts (120 seconds)
Step 20. Place the letter inside the envelope (15 seconds)

Step 22. Check the ink for smudges (30 seconds)
Step 23. Set the finished letter aside to dry (600 seconds)

Step 26. Write your return address (45 seconds)

Step 30. Blow on the signature to ensure it is dry (30 seconds)
Step 31. Buy a fresh pack of envelopes (3600 seconds)
Step 32. Check the mail collection times (120 seconds)
Step 33. Ensure the zip code is legible (30 seconds)
Step 34. Drop the letter into the slot (5 seconds)
Step 35. Center the address on the envelope (30 seconds)
Step 36. Peel a stamp from the roll (10 seconds)
Step 37. Read a previous letter for context (600 seconds)
Step 38. Think of a funny anecdote to include (300 seconds)
Step 39. Affix the stamp to the top right corner (15 seconds)
Step 40. Look up the recipient's new house number (240 seconds)

Step 42. Press the stamp down firmly (5 seconds)
Step 43. Smooth out any wrinkles in the paper (10 seconds)
Step 44. Close the mailbox door (5 seconds)

Step 49. Choose which color of ink to use (60 seconds)
Step 50. Ensure the letter is not too heavy for one stamp (120 seconds)
Step 51. Look for the roll of clear tape (240 seconds)
Step 52. Select a high-quality envelope (30 seconds)
Step 53. Calculate the total cost of the stationery (300 seconds)
Step 54. Moistening the adhesive strip (5 seconds)
Step 55. Count the number of pages used (15 seconds)
Step 56. Double-check that the envelope is flat (10 seconds)
Step 57. Test the pen on a scrap piece of paper (30 seconds)
Step 58. Walk back to your front door (600 seconds)
Step 59. Put the cap back on the pen (5 seconds)
Step 60. Underline important phrases for emphasis (120 seconds)
Step 61. Gather all necessary writing materials (360 seconds)
Step 62. Put on your shoes and coat (180 seconds)
Step 63. Choose a quiet place to write (300 seconds)
Step 64. Check the weather forecast for the walk (120 seconds)
Step 65. Grab your keys from the hook (60 seconds)
Step 66. Check that the letter is actually in your pocket (10 seconds)
Step 67. Wash your hands to avoid staining the paper (180 seconds)
Step 68. Pick out a specific stamp design (60 seconds)
Step 69. Clean your glasses for better vision (60 seconds)
Step 70. Mention a mutual friend in the text (120 seconds)
Step 71. Confirm the mailbox is not overflowing (30 seconds)
Step 72. Double-check the date (10 seconds)
Step 73. Verify the street name spelling (120 seconds)
Step 74. Wet the sponge for the envelope seal (30 seconds)
Step 75. Slide the letter carefully into the sleeve (15 seconds)
Step 76. Ensure the stamp is not upside down (10 seconds)
Step 77. Check the house number one last time (30 seconds)
Step 78. Clear your schedule for the afternoon (1200 seconds)
Step 79. Walk to the edge of the sidewalk (120 seconds)
Step 80. Look for any "No Parking" signs near the box (60 seconds)
Step 81. Note the time you sent the letter (60 seconds)
Step 82. Double-check the envelope for a return address (30 seconds)
Step 83. Sit down at the writing desk (60 seconds)
Step 84. Draft a concluding sentence (180 seconds)
Step 85. Check that the envelope is not torn (15 seconds)
Step 86. Add a second stamp if necessary (20 seconds)
Step 87. Verify the mailbox location on a map (300 seconds)
Step 88. Take a deep breath of fresh air (10 seconds)
Step 89. Check your watch for the time (10 seconds)
Step 90. Re-read the letter one last time (300 seconds)
Step 91. Hear the letter hit the bottom of the bin (2 seconds)
Step 92. Think about what the recipient will feel (240 seconds)
Step 93. Find a flat surface to press the seal (60 seconds)
Step 94. Ensure the recipient's name is legible (30 seconds)
Step 95. Verify the postage is sufficient (120 seconds)
Step 96. Check for any loose edges on the envelope (20 seconds)
Step 97. Look for any missed spots of glue (30 seconds)
Step 98. Lick the envelope flap (5 seconds)
Step 99. Wave to a neighbor on the street (15 seconds)
Step 100. Feel a sense of accomplishment (60 seconds)
